sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 23.1 for China (band 15.0–40.6, from 3 of six components) and 38.3 for the United States (band 33.6–69.7, from 4 of six components). The net lean is -15.2 points toward the United States.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China was broadly flat and the index for the United States rose by 26.5 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 0.0% of Panama's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$341 m) went to China and 0.0% to the United States; together 0.0%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China fell by 59.2 points and the share going to the United States fell by 4.3 points.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in copper (RCA 2.1).
1 sudden shift in export shares is flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2021: Exports to China fell from 66% to 39% of copper exports between 2020 and 2021 (reported by PAN to UN Comtrade).
The AidData records show US$576 m of documented commitments from Chinese institutions to Panama over 2002–2020 (33 events; the source ends in 2021).
The DFC and EXIM records show US$282 m of documented commitments from US institutions to Panama over 2007–2026 (143 events).

The lenders with the largest recorded commitments to named recipients here are Export-Import Bank of China (China Eximbank) (US$269 m), OPIC (predecessor of DFC) (US$221 m) and China Development Bank (CDB) (US$120 m).
In the UN General Assembly, voting agreement in 2024 was 68% with China and 50% with the United States.
Since 2019, agreement with China fell by 13.6 points and agreement with the United States rose by 22.7 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After China: exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States prohibited (Announcement 2024 No. 46) (2024-12), the share of exports to China moved -45.8 points (46% before, 0.0% after); placebo p 0.09 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on antimony items in force (Announcement 2024 No. 33 of 15 August 2024) (2024-09), the share of exports to China moved -45.8 points (46% before, 0.0% after); placebo p 0.09 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on graphite items in force (Announcement 2023 No. 39 of 20 October 2023) (2023-12), the share of exports to China moved -39.9 points (40% before, 0.0% after); placebo p 0.14 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 26.1 (90% band 1.5–46.5), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 38.4 (90% band 5.1–71.4), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 3% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
12 of the dated events used above are still in the draft event list awaiting the project owner's review.
Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.

speaker.name: Felipe Chapman
speaker.role: Minister of Economy and Finance of Panama

records.event_context: Delivery of Interministerial Commission final report on Cobre Panamá site
records.summary_en: Chapman said any solution for the Cobre Panamá site must cost the state budget nothing.
records.quote_original: Cero es lo que debe costar al Presupuesto General del Estado.
records.quote_en: Zero is what it must cost the General State Budget.

source.name: Presidencia de la República de Panamá

records.event_context: Delivery of Interministerial Commission final report on Cobre Panamá site
records.summary_en: Mulino received the commission's final report, set six non-negotiable criteria (respect for the Court ruling, state sovereignty over minerals, zero fiscal cost, transparency, community priority, international supervision) and said he would not rush a decision.
records.quote_original: Esos seis no se negocian. Todo lo demás se estudia.
records.quote_en: Those six are not negotiable. Everything else will be studied.

source.name: Presidencia de la República de Panamá

records.event_context: Delivery of Interministerial Commission final report on Cobre Panamá site
records.summary_en: Navarro said inaction at the mine site is not an option and that closure must be independently verified rather than declared by the company doing the closing.
records.quote_original: Lo que está prohibido es NO HACER NADA.
records.quote_en: What is forbidden is to DO NOTHING.

source.name: Presidencia de la República de Panamá

speaker.name: Julio Moltó
speaker.role: Minister of Commerce and Industries of Panama

records.event_context: Delivery of Interministerial Commission final report on Cobre Panamá site
records.summary_en: Moltó argued that indefinite indecision on the mine is the costliest option and is paid by the most vulnerable citizens, citing lost foreign exchange and jobs.
records.quote_original: la más costosa de todas, y la pagan los ciudadanos más vulnerables
records.quote_en: the costliest of all, and it is paid by the most vulnerable citizens

source.name: Presidencia de la República de Panamá

records.event_context: Approval to process stockpiled ore at Cobre Panamá
records.summary_en: The government approved removal, processing and export of ~38 Mt of stockpiled ore at Cobre Panamá to fund preservation and reduce environmental risks, stressing this was not a reopening of the mine.
records.notes: Corporate source; Wikipedia gives January 2026 for authorization – date discrepancy, release dated 2026-04-07.

speaker.name: José W. Fernández
speaker.role: U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Growth, Energy, and the Environment

records.event_context: Reuters interview on First Quantum's Cobre Panamá dispute
records.related_entities: Cobre Panamá; First Quantum Minerals; Minerals Security Partnership
records.summary_en: Fernández said the future of the closed Cobre Panamá copper mine was for Panamanians to decide and that communities must be convinced they will benefit from mining, while promoting the US-led minerals partnership as an alternative to Chinese-dominated supply chains.
records.quote_original: We have followed the case, and it is an issue for the Panamanian people to decide
records.quote_en: We have followed the case, and it is an issue for the Panamanian people to decide
records.notes: Interview given late Monday 4 Mar 2024, published 5 Mar. China dominance point is reporter context; stance_china neutral.

speaker.role: Minister of Commerce and Industries of Panama

records.summary_en: The nine Supreme Court justices unanimously declared Law 406 approving the Cobre Panamá contract unconstitutional, citing violations of 25 constitutional articles; the ruling was published in the Official Gazette on 2 Dec 2023.
records.notes: Unanimity and 25 articles per Wikipedia citing AP; Gaceta Oficial 29685-D.

records.summary_en: Cortizo said his administration would comply with the ruling and ensure a safe and orderly closure of the Cobre Panamá mine, beginning the transition process.
records.notes: Details via Wikipedia '2023 Panamanian protests' summary citing this article; the article itself could not be fetched (site blocked). English paraphrase only.

records.summary_en: The Assembly approved an indefinite moratorium on new metallic mining concessions (Bill 1110, Law 407) after removing an amendment that would have repealed Law 406; Cortizo signed it the same day.
records.notes: Final approval/signature per Wikipedia citing AP (https://apnews.com/article/panama-bill-mine-moratorium-protests-environment-canada-3ed264e871f09fa5ee7ed6fb6eeb0c61).

records.summary_en: Facing mass protests, Cortizo proposed a national referendum on whether to keep the Cobre Panamá contract (Bill 1109).
records.notes: Details via Wikipedia '2023 Panamanian protests' summary citing this article; the article itself could not be fetched (site blocked). Bill 1109 first debate 2023-10-31 confirmed in First Quantum update of 2023-11-03.

records.summary_en: Cortizo signed into law the renewed First Quantum concession contract hours after the National Assembly approved it in third debate, triggering nationwide protests.
